clinicalPearls: X-linked recessive proximal tubulopathy caused by OCRL variants, the same gene responsible for Lowe (oculocerebrorenal) syndrome.
Represents the milder end of the OCRL phenotypic spectrum, combining a Dent-like renal picture with subtle extrarenal features.
Low-molecular-weight proteinuria, for example of beta-2-microglobulin, retinol-binding protein and alpha-1-microglobulin, is the biochemical hallmark.
Hypercalciuria with nephrocalcinosis and/or nephrolithiasis is common, alongside variable features of generalised proximal tubular dysfunction.
Mild extrarenal features may include subclinical lens opacities, mild intellectual impairment, hypotonia and modestly raised muscle enzymes, distinguishing Dent 2 from CLCN5-related Dent disease 1.
Progressive chronic kidney disease may develop, with a proportion of males reaching end-stage in adulthood.
Female carriers are usually asymptomatic or have only mild low-molecular-weight proteinuria.
OCRL accounts for a minority of Dent disease; most cases are CLCN5-related Dent disease 1.
reference.pathophysiology: OCRL on chromosome Xq26.1 encodes OCRL-1, a phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 5-phosphatase that localises to the Golgi apparatus, endosomes and the primary cilium and regulates membrane trafficking and the actin cytoskeleton, functions that are critical to the endocytic machinery of the renal proximal tubule. Loss of enzyme function disturbs the megalin-cubilin receptor-mediated endocytosis by which the proximal tubule reclaims filtered low-molecular-weight proteins, producing the characteristic low-molecular-weight proteinuria together with hypercalciuria and broader proximal tubular dysfunction. The severity depends on the specific variant and its effect on the protein: hypomorphic OCRL variants, often affecting particular domains, cause the comparatively mild renal-predominant Dent disease 2, whereas more damaging variants produce the full oculocerebrorenal syndrome of Lowe with congenital cataracts, neurological impairment and tubulopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Lowe (oculocerebrorenal) syndrome, the severe OCRL end of the spectrum
Other causes of renal Fanconi syndrome (cystinosis, Wilson disease, tyrosinaemia, galactosaemia, mitochondrial cytopathies)

Urinary calcium excretion, as a calcium-to-creatinine ratio or timed collection
Renal ultrasound for nephrocalcinosis and stones

Molecular genetic testing of OCRL, with CLCN5 testing to distinguish Dent disease 1
redFlags: Symptomatic nephrolithiasis or urinary tract obstruction
Bone disease or rickets from phosphate wasting
reference.prognosis: The course is slowly progressive; a proportion of affected males develop end-stage renal disease in adulthood, while the extrarenal features remain milder than those of Lowe syndrome.
pitfalls: Low-molecular-weight proteinuria may be misread as glomerular proteinuria, prompting inappropriate immunosuppression.
The disorder may be mislabelled as idiopathic hypercalciuria or nephrotic syndrome.
Absence of a family history does not exclude it, given carrier mothers and de novo variants.
The subtle extrarenal features that separate Dent 2 from Dent 1 are easily missed.
references: Standard paediatric and adult nephrology texts
Reviews of the Dent disease spectrum
management: No disease-specific therapy; reduce hypercalciuria with thiazide diuretics and maintain generous hydration to limit nephrocalcinosis and stone formation
Replace proximal tubular losses of phosphate, potassium and alkali and treat metabolic bone disease with vitamin D and phosphate supplementation
Slow chronic kidney disease progression with blood-pressure control and avoidance of nephrotoxins
Surveillance with serial kidney function, low-molecular-weight proteinuria, urinary calcium and renal ultrasound
Slit-lamp ophthalmology review for lens opacities and monitoring of mild neurodevelopmental and muscle involvement that distinguish the OCRL phenotype
Provide renal replacement therapy and transplantation for kidney failure with nephrology multidisciplinary input
Offer X-linked genetic counselling and screen at-risk relatives
